## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Static HTML project. Let me design the game thoroughly.

## Concept
**"SAKURA ROYALE"** — 2D anime battle royale, top-down. 20 players (you + 19 bots) on an island, shrinking storm circle. Collect scrolls (power-ups), fight with anime abilities. Last one standing wins.

Visual style: anime / cel-shaded, pastel cherry blossoms, floating petals, vibrant. Characters drawn procedurally: chibi characters with hair, big eyes, weapons. Distinct character skins/colors, names (anime-ish).

## Technical plan
Files:
- `index.html` — shell, HUD DOM, menus
- `css/style.css` — UI, responsive
- `js/` modules:
  - `main.js` — bootstrap, screens, game loop
  - `game.js` — world, entities, simulation
  - `render.js` — drawing
  - `audio.js` — procedural SFX/music
  - `input.js` — touch joystick + keyboard/mouse
  - `characters.js` — character defs & sprites

Or to keep simpler but still organized, maybe 4-5 files. ES modules work with static server.

Mobile-first: Portrait & landscape support. Full-screen canvas with DPR scaling. Touch controls:
- Left virtual joystick (dynamic — appears where thumb touches in left zone) for movement
- Right: attack button (auto-aim at nearest enemy), dash button, skill button (special character skill)
- Auto-aim shooting for accessibility. Also mouse aim on desktop, WASD + click.

Game mechanics:
- HP 100, shield
- Weapons: Each character has primary ranged projectile (ki blast etc.), melee range for some. Simpler: primary auto-fire projectile toward nearest enemy within range when holding attack (or auto-fire toggle).
- Abilities: character-specific:
  1. **Hana (Samurai)** — Crescent Slash: 3-blade wave cone, high damage short range.
  2. **Rin (Mage)** — Frost Nova: AoE around self, slows.
  3. **Kaze (Ninja)** — Shadow Dash: dash + damage trail, invisibility brief.
  4. **Mei (Gunner)** — Missile Barrage: homing rockets.
  5. **Yuki (Healer/Spirit)** — Healing Bloom / barrier.
  Player selects one at start.
- Power-ups on map: health rice balls (+30), shield onigiri, damage up (scroll), speed up (tabi), and "awakening" star.
- Storm: circular safe zone shrinking in phases with timer; outside damage ramps.
- Bots: state machine — seek loot, engage enemies, flee to zone, use skills. Bots fight each other, so player count decreases organically. Off-screen bots eliminated via simplified combat resolution? Better: simulate all bots in world even off-screen; update cheap. 19 bots fine. Camera culls rendering.
- Kill feed notifications, floating damage numbers, hit particles, screen shake.
- Match flow: menu → character select → match → results.
- Minimap in HUD corner showing zone circle + players (only nearby? show all for clarity).
- Victory: rank #1 "VICTORY ROYALE" style "LAST ONE STANDING".

Rendering polish is key. Anime aesthetic:
- Soft gradient background (island grass: teal-green with subtle pattern), cherry blossom trees, rocks, koi ponds?
- Draw ground with pastel gradient, scattered petals drifting, ambient light.
- Characters: chibi proportions — head big, body small, hair shapes, face, weapon. Directional facing with slight bob animation, run cycle (legs).
- Shadows (ellipse).
- Attack effects: glowing crescent slashes, energy orbs with trails, particle bursts.
- Vignette + color grading.

Let me be careful about scope: the code will be large but manageable (~2500-3500 lines total). I have good token budget. Let's structure:

1. `index.html` (~150 lines)
2. `css/style.css` (~600 lines) — polished UI
3. `js/characters.js` (~200)
4. `js/input.js` (~200)
5. `js/audio.js` (~250)
6. `js/world.js` (~900) — simulation
7. `js/render.js` (~800)
8. `js/main.js` (~500) — screens, loop, HUD

Must ensure performance on mobile: canvas drawing with many entities; use simple shapes, limit particles (~400), culling.

Let me think about mobile layout & controls carefully:
- Game area full viewport; use `100dvh`, `env(safe-area-inset-*)`.
- Canvas sized to window * DPR capped at 2.
- Camera zoom based on viewport min dimension: want world visible ~900 units wide on phone. zoom = min(w,h)/520? Let's define world units; player radius 18, map 3200x3200. On phone (390x844 portrait), zoom maybe 1.1 (visible 355x767 world units) — too zoomed. Let's set camera scale = clamp(min(vw,vh)/560, 0.55, 1.1)? For 390 wide: 390/560 = 0.696 → visible 560x1213 world units. Reasonable. Desktop 1440x900: min=900/560=1.607 → clamp 1.1, visible 1309x818. Fine.
- Portrait works but landscape better. Add "rotate device" hint? Not necessary; support both. Actually on phone portrait, a top-down game with controls at bottom is fine.

Controls:
- Left half: movement joystick (appears on touchstart, anchored).
- Right side buttons: ATK (big, bottom-right), DASH (above-left of ATK), SKILL (above ATK?). Simpler layout: two circles: attack (biggest) at bottom-right; skill left of it; dash above attack. Auto-aim means just hold attack.
- Actually for satisfying play: attack is auto-fired when enemy in range? Many mobile BR games require aiming. Let's do: primary fires automatically at nearest enemy in range while "ATK" held OR always auto-fire toggle... Hmm. To make it accessible: hold ATK to fire; aim assist targets nearest enemy in ~360 range; if none, fire in facing direction. That's fine. Also auto-fire option? Let default auto-attack ON to reduce burden: "AUTO" toggle in HUD. I'll implement auto-fire always on when enemy in range, plus manual hold to extend? Might confuse.

Better: Attack button = fire; but also enable "auto-fire" checkbox in menu (default on). Auto-fire shoots every weapon cooldown at nearest enemy within detection range. Then attack button becomes "Aim burst"? Simpler: single ATK button fires; when held, continuous; a slight aim assist. Game can be played with left thumb move + right thumb hold attack. Skill + dash are extra. That's standard.

To reduce difficulty, bots not too lethal, and player has shield regen? Keep health packs.

Bots: 19. Each has character type, skill usage, accuracy variance. They move around, seek zone, pick loot, fight nearest within 260 units. Damaging each other.

Player count: start 20, show alive counter. Kill feed.

Zone: map 3200. Center random-ish (0,0). Phases:
- Phase 0: wait 25s, radius 1650 (whole map-ish)
- Phase 1: shrink 20s to 1150
- Phase 2: 18s → 780
- Phase 3: 16s → 500
- Phase 4: 14s → 300
- Phase 5: 12s → 150
- Final: radius 60 then 0?
Outside damage: 2 + phase*2.5 per second.

Time to first blood ~ bots engage quickly. Match ~2-3 min. Good.

Loot: ~55 crates scattered, types: heal, shield, damage, speed, skill charge? Also weapon upgrade? Keep: health (+35), shield (+40 up to 60), power (+15% dmg, stack 3), speed, and "star" grants full skill charge and heals.

Characters & skills:
- **HANA** (Samurai, pink) — Primary: petal slash projectile (short range, wide). Skill: "Crescent Storm" — three expanding crescent waves, 40 dmg each, knockback.
- **RIN** (Frost mage, blue) — Primary: ice shard (fast, small). Skill: "Glacier Bloom" — AoE circle around self, 35 dmg + slow 50% 3s.
- **KAZE** (Ninja, purple) — Primary: kunai (fast). Skill: "Shadow Step" — dash forward 320 units, damaging enemies passed (45), brief invuln.
- **MEI** (Gunner, orange) — Primary: rapid bolts (fast fire). Skill: "Cherry Blossom Barrage" — 6 homing missiles.
- **YUKI** (Spirit, mint) — Primary: spirit orb (medium). Skill: "Lunar Veil" — heals 30 + shield 40 and pulse damage 25.
- **RYU**? Maybe 5 is enough. Unlock? Keep 5.

Stats vary: speed, hp, fire rate, damage.

Render characters distinct: hair color, outfit color, accessory (headband, hat, etc.), weapon shape. Add names above heads? For enemies show small name/HP bar; player has ring marker.

Anime aesthetic touches:
- Opening title with big Japanese-ish typography "桜のバトルロイヤル" subtitle.
- Backgrounds: gradient sky? Top-down so ground; add decorative cherry trees with pink canopies casting shadows; stone lanterns; wooden bridges; pond with koi? Keep decorative props: trees, rocks, flower patches, torii gates. Collision? Skip prop collision for smoothness, or add collision for rocks/trees? Battle royale needs open movement; skip collision except map bounds. Trees drawn behind/above entities (canopy overlay) for depth—maybe avoid overlay complexity; draw props shadows beneath and canopies above characters for trees player can walk under. Nice depth. But risk hiding player. Use semi-transparent canopies. I'll draw canopies at 0.85 alpha above entities. Actually might obscure fights. Draw trees with canopy under entity layer? Then characters walk over canopy weird. Compromise: draw trunk + canopy behind entities (flat, perspective top-down), with shadow. Fine.

Effects:
- Petals drifting globally (screen-space).
- Hit sparks, damage numbers, death explosion (petals + light).
- Trail for projectiles.
- Storm visual: outside zone darkened purple with animated edge and lightning.

HUD:
- Top-left: alive count + kills.
- Top-center: zone timer/progress.
- Top-right: pause + sound buttons.
- Bottom-left: joystick zone.
- Right: buttons.
- Minimap: top-right under buttons? Maybe top-left under alive? Common: minimap top-right. On phones top-right could overlap pause. Put minimap bottom-right? Buttons there. Hmm. Put minimap at top-right below pause/sound row, size 110-140px.
- HP bar above bottom center or near player? BR games have bottom-center. Add player HP + shield bar bottom-center (above joystick line). Buttons bottom-right, joystick bottom-left. Centered bar is clear.
- Skill charge / cooldown ring on button.

Screens:
- Title screen: logo, "TAP TO PLAY", buttons: Play, How to Play, sound.
- Character select: cards horizontally scrollable, each with preview drawing on canvas or CSS art. Show stats and skill. "BATTLE" button.
- Results: rank, kills, damage, time survived, buttons "Play Again" / "Change Hero".
- Pause modal: resume, quit, sound.
- Tutorial overlay (first time) or "How to Play" panel with controls.

Use DOM for screens; canvas game behind. Character preview: draw avatar on small canvas per card using render function (expose drawPortrait). Or CSS gradient + emoji? Better use canvas portrait for quality. I can render character in each card canvas via a portrait renderer.

Implementation details:

Coordinate system: world units, player pos. Use delta time capped.

Entity struct:
```js
{ id, bot, charId, name, x, y, vx, vy, angle, hp, maxHp, shield, speed, ... }
```

Combat:
- Projectiles: {x,y,vx,vy,r,dmg,owner,team,kind,life,homing,color,trail[]}
- Melee/AoE: instant effects list.
- Collision: circle distance; projectiles hit nearest enemy; friendly fire off.
- Bots perceive enemies: nearest alive other. Move toward if far, strafe if in range.
- Player: auto-aim toward nearest enemy for firing? For projectile direction, use aim vector: nearest enemy within 380 if aim assist, else facing. Camera doesn't rotate.
- Manual aim on desktop: mouse position gives facing; clicking fires. On touch: right side drag could aim... but buttons. Auto-aim assist is enough.

Bots decision:
- Every ~0.15-0.4s choose target; move: if outside zone → head to center; if hp low → seek health pickup or flee; else engage at preferred range (char.range), strafe.
- Fire with cooldown, accuracy jitter.
- Use skill when cooldown ready and enemy near.
- Bots also collect loot when passing.
- Bots kill each other; ensure matches end (zone damage). Final circle forces fights.

Balance: To make the game fun/win-able, player damage advantage slight, bots have reaction delay when targeting player. Also bots fight among themselves often.

Potential issue: bots at 19 entities, each shooting; performance fine.
